posts.caption:
Perimenopause often catches us off guard—but the hormonal story starts before the hot flushes. Progesterone is usually the first to decline, and it's the workhorse keeping inflammation in check, anxiety at bay, and histamine stable.

In susceptible women, this shift can trigger real changes: brain fog, sleep disruption, joint achiness, even new food sensitivities. The good news? Understanding the *why* helps us respond more strategically—through nutrition, stress management, and targeted investigation.

If you're noticing patterns through your cycle or suspect you're in early perimenopause, let's map it together and work out what your body actually needs right now.

Book a consultation to discuss your hormonal patterns.

#Perimenopause #ProgesteroneMatters #FunctionalMedicine #HormoneHealth #WomensHealth

- Whitespace & density: Generous negative space around the clinician, text anchored to lower third, uncluttered composition. Green banner as the sole chromatic anchor; everything else warm and neutral.
- Reel voice/script: Hook frame (1–2 sec) introduces [headline], then pivots to 2–3 beat spoken question or statement ([supporting question], [evidence-based insight], [curiosity prompt]). Warm, clinical, never alarmist.

COLOUR PALETTE (green-anchored, harmonising):
- Primary anchor: EHN green #39B54A (banner, accent word, visual focus).
- Background: Warm cream, soft sage-grey, soft charcoal, or a muted colour that complements green (never pure white, never pure black, never the competitor's specific palette). Feels warm, editorial, clinical.
- Text (body): White on green banner (high contrast). Charcoal or warm neutral on cream/background (warm, readable).
- Accents: None competing — green is the sole chromatic anchor; all other elements neutral or warm tones.

TYPOGRAPHY (LOCKED):
- Headline [keyword]: Satoshi Bold, one meaningful word in green #39B54A italic, oversized (~95px relative hierarchy on 1080 canvas). Rest in bold charcoal or neutral.
- Credential/supporting line (banner): Satoshi Medium, white, body-sized (~40–50px equivalent hierarchy), clear and legible.
- Reel voiceover: conversational, warm, Australian plain-English tone.

LEGIBILITY FLOORS (HARD):
- Headline text >=36px (enforce via relative hierarchy, not absolute point size).
- Body/credential text >=40px (enforce via hierarchy).
- Headline equivalent ~95px+ (relative to 1080 canvas).
- Rule: SHORTEN COPY, NEVER SHRINK THE FONT. If voiceover or credential line is too long, cut words, don't reduce size.

BRAND & CTA:
- Logo (small, unobtrusive) in corner or fade-out at end-frame.
- Reel CTA: Soft prompt ("Learn more", "Book a consultation", "Tap the link") — no hypey language.
- Brand close: "Elemental Health & Nutrition" on lower-third banner or in end-frame. NEVER the suburb name on the card.

FEEL & TONE:
- Clinical but warm, intimate, grounded, editorial. Australian-natural aesthetic (sage, cream, charcoal, warm tones). No stock-wellness clichés. Authority + approachability via the clinician's direct gaze and warm setting.

posts.caption:
Do you bloat after meals, even when you're eating 'well'? Feel foggy or tired a couple of hours after food? Your gut bacteria might be telling you something.

Small intestinal bacterial overgrowth (SIBO) happens when bacteria that normally live lower in your gut move upstream and start fermenting your meals. It's not a diagnosis we chase lightly, but when symptoms like bloating, fatigue and food sensitivity cluster together, it's worth investigating.

The good news: a functional-medicine approach looks at **why** this happened in the first place — stress, food sensitivities, low stomach acid, previous infection — not just treating the symptom.

If this resonates, let's chat about your digestion. Book an appointment to explore what's really going on.

#GutHealth #SIBO #FunctionalMedicine #AdelaideClinic #DigestionSupport #Bloating #FoodsensitivityAware
